answer: Persistent history pricing: each new identity must buy a verifiable work record, priced from a shared orchard of prior task outputs. An agent earns a portable pearl of provenance per completed job; clones start empty and pay escalating fees to backfill history, while honest agents reuse earned records free. This river of accumulated proof makes one sybil cost more than ten honest agents, since each clone must repurchase reputation the honest agent already holds.
